text.en:
After heavy rain, water filled Seema's street. Her family had no gas for cooking.
The neighbours shared food and gave her baby brother milk. Young people helped carry old people to dry places.
"We are a family, and the street is our community," Seema's grandfather said.

A family is a group of people who live together and care for each other. A nuclear family has parents and children. A joint family has several generations living together, such as grandparents, parents, uncles, aunts and cousins.
A family gives us love, food, shelter, safety and our first lessons about right and wrong. Each member has a role, and we help each other.
A community is a group of people living in the same area or sharing the same interests, such as neighbours in a street, a village or a school. Communities work together on festivals, cleanliness and in times of trouble.
We belong to many communities: family, school, neighbourhood, village or town, and country.
Good communities depend on cooperation, respect, sharing and responsibility.
A family is a group that lives together and cares for each other.
A nuclear family has parents and children. A joint family has many relatives together.
A community is a group living in one area, like a street, a village or a school.
Good communities share, cooperate, and help each other in trouble.

problem.en: Name two ways a community helps its members.

text.en: Neighbours help each other in trouble, such as floods.
People share festivals, water and safety.
So communities help through cooperation and sharing.

prompt.en: A friend says it is not his job to keep the street clean. What will you say?

requiredIdeas.en: The street is shared by the whole community.
When everyone does a little, the street stays clean for all.

points.en: Families can be nuclear or joint.
A community is a group living together or sharing interests.
